questions.q: A food item contains 15 grams of carbohydrates, 10 grams of protein, and 5 grams of fat. What is the total caloric value of this food?
questions.explain: Calculation: $(15\text{g CHO} \times 4\text{ kcal/g}) + (10\text{g PRO} \times 4\text{ kcal/g}) + (5\text{g FAT} \times 9\text{ kcal/g}) = 60 + 40 + 45 = 145\text{ kcal}$.

questions.q: If a diet provides 2000 kcal per day and 30% of energy comes from fat, how many grams of fat should be consumed?
questions.explain: Calculation: $2000\text{ kcal} \times 0.30 = 600\text{ kcal from fat}$. Then, $600\text{ kcal} / 9\text{ kcal/g} \approx 66.67\text{g}$. Round to 67g.

questions.q: The Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Range (AMDR) for carbohydrates is 45-65%. For a 2400 kcal diet, what is the *minimum* recommended grams of carbohydrate?
questions.explain: Minimum % is 45%. $2400\text{ kcal} \times 0.45 = 1080\text{ kcal from CHO}$. Convert to grams: $1080\text{ kcal} / 4\text{ kcal/g} = 270\text{ grams}$.

questions.q: A snack bar lists the following nutrition facts: Total Fat 6g, Total Carbohydrate 24g (Dietary Fiber 4g), Protein 10g. Calculate the *percentage* of calories derived from protein. (Round to nearest whole number).
questions.explain: Total kcal = $(6\times9) + (24\times4) + (10\times4) = 54 + 96 + 40 = 190\text{ kcal}$. Protein kcal = $40$. Percentage = $(40 / 190) \times 100 \approx 21.05\%$. Answer is 21%.

questions.q: Calculate the calories provided by a meal containing 12g of Saturated Fat, 14g of Monounsaturated Fat, 4g of Polyunsaturated Fat, 40g of Starch, and 20g of Protein.
questions.explain: Total Fat = $12+14+4 = 30\text{g}$. Total Fat kcal = $30 \times 9 = 270$. Carbohydrate (Starch) kcal = $40 \times 4 = 160$. Protein kcal = $20 \times 4 = 80$. Total = $270 + 160 + 80 = 510\text{ kcal}$.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Carbohydrates, Proteins, and Fats
questions.subject: HOSA Nutrition

questions.q: If a patient requires 25 kcal/kg of body weight and weighs 80 kg, and they are restricted to 0.8g protein per kg, how many calories per day remain for carbohydrates and fats?
questions.explain: Total needs = $80\text{kg} \times 25\text{ kcal/kg} = 2000\text{ kcal}$. Protein allocation = $80\text{kg} \times 0.8\text{g/kg} = 64\text{g}$. Protein kcal = $64 \times 4 = 256\text{ kcal}$. Remaining kcal = $2000 - 256 = 1744\text{ kcal}$.
